previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with metastatic cholangiocarcinoma and a history of recurrent cholangitis due to multidrug-resistant E. coli, was admitted with fevers and decreased output from his percutaneous transhepatic biliary drain (PTBD) following an iron infusion. Blood cultures confirmed MDR E. coli bacteremia, and imaging showed stable liver microabscesses with a clogged PTBD. He underwent PTBD exchange with upsizing of the catheter to improve drainage. Initial treatment with ceftazidime-avibactam, metronidazole, and planned tobramycin and tigecycline was adjusted when cultures showed sensitivity to meropenem; he was transitioned to meropenem and tigecycline, later changed to ertapenem for outpatient administration. A new PICC line was placed for IV antibiotics. He had a brief episode of bloody PTBD output after straining, which resolved spontaneously. He tolerated a PTBD capping trial and was discharged home with capped drain, on IV ertapenem and tigecycline, with plans for weekly labs, follow-up MRI, and infectious disease evaluation to determine treatment duration.

Marrow signal elsewhere is normal.  The distal spinal cord and conus
medullaris is normal and terminates at T12-L1.  The cauda equina nerve roots
are unremarkable.  There is no epidural collection.

Signal height loss of lumbar spine intervertebral discs is consistent with
degenerative change.  Nonspecific facet joint fluid is noted at multiple
levels of the lumbar spine.   There is a posterior annular fissure at L2-3. 
Disc height loss worst at L5-S1. disc bulges, ligamentum flavum thickening,
and facet osteophytes cause varying degrees of spinal canal and neural
foraminal narrowing.  Specifically:

T12-L1: There is no definite evidence of vertebral canal or neural foraminal
narrowing.
L1-2: Mild bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.
L2-3: Mild-to-moderate spinal canal narrowing.  Mild left neural narrowing.
L3-4: Mild spinal canal and left subarticular zone narrowing, possible contact
of the descending left nerve root.  Mild right and moderate left neural
narrowing.
L4-5: Mild to moderate spinal canal narrowing, narrowing the right
subarticular zone, possible contact of the descending right L5 nerve root. 
Mild-to-moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.
L5-S1: No spinal canal narrowing.  Mild right and moderate left neural
foraminal narrowing.

 OTHER:

There are T2 hyperintensities in the renal cortices bilaterally, largest in
the left measuring 2 cm, incompletely characterized.  Mildly trabeculated
bladder wall is noted, nonspecific.

IMPRESSION:


1.  Study is moderately degraded by motion.
2. 17 mm enhancing lesion centered in the right anterolateral L3 vertebral
body with an extra osseous component is concerning for metastasis, with
degenerative change less likely.
3. Multilevel lumbar spondylosis as described.  Spinal canal narrowing is
worst (mild-to-moderate) at L2-3 and L4-5.  Neural foraminal narrowing is
worst (moderate) on the left at L3-4 and L5-S1.
4. Additional findings as described.

EXAMINATION:  MRI of the Abdomen

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with inoperable cholangiocarcinoma evaluating for
disease progression// evaluate for disease progression

TECHNIQUE:  T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet.
Intravenous contrast: Gadavist.

COMPARISON:  Prior MR abdomen done ___ and prior lumbar spine MR
done ___

FINDINGS: 

The study is markedly degraded by motion artifact.

Lower Thorax: There is no pleural or pericardial effusion.

Liver: Similar to the prior study, there is diffuse atrophy of the left
hepatic segments.  Peripheral area of fibrosis and volume loss within segment
6 appear similar compared to prior (series 4, image 32).  The previously
suspected nonocclusive thrombus in relation to the right posterior portal vein
just beyond the stent as well as the thrombus within a segment 5 portal venous
branch as result.  The previously noted rim enhancing hepatic abscess in
segment 8 is no longer visualized.  PTB in situ though coursing through the
right anterior segment.  Perihepatic edema as well as mild enhancement about
the PTB is most likely reactive.

Biliary: Double CBD stents coursing into the right and left hepatic ducts in
situ.  Intrinsic T1 hyperintense material in the CBD stent (series 9, image
70) most likely represents reflux of oral contrast.  Marked edema and
enhancement surrounding the stents in the central aspect of the liver (series
1101, image 60 and 61) suggest acute on chronic cholangitis change.  Dilated
segment 5 ducts appear similar compared to prior.  Left hepatic biliary ductal
dilatation within the atrophic left lobe appear similar compared to prior.

Pancreas: Pancreatic atrophy with mild duct dilatation appear stable.  There
is millimetric cystic lesions present in the pancreatic tail, similar compared
to prior.

Spleen: Splenomegaly measuring up to 16 cm.  No focal suspicious splenic
lesions.

Adrenal Glands: Unremarkable

Kidneys: Simple renal cystic lesions are noted.  No hydronephrosis or
suspicious renal lesions

Gastrointestinal Tract:  No bowel obstruction.  Gastric mucosal thickening may
represent portal gastropathy.

Lymph Nodes: No lymphadenopathy

Vasculature: Major vasculature are patent.  The portal venous stent appears
patent.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: Indeterminate enhancing L3 vertebral body
lesion (series 5, image 26 and series 1103, image 133) was better
characterized on prior lumbar spine MRI.


IMPRESSION: 

The previously seen hepatic microabscesses have resolved.  There is no new or
worsening intrahepatic infection.

Interval resolution of the non-occlusive thrombus within the right posterior
portal vein as well as the segment 5 portal venous branch.

Double biliary stents in situ with surrounding edema and enhancement in
keeping with acute on chronic cholangitis changes.  Stable left hepatic lobe
atrophy and PTBD.

Splenomegaly, as before.

Indeterminate L3 vertebral body lesion was better characterized on prior
lumbar spine MRI and reference is made to that report.

ADDENDUM  The procedure should state:
PROCEDURE:
CT-guided L3 paravertebral body soft tissue biopsy

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cholangiocarcinoma, with new L3 lesion
concerning for malignancy.// Biopsy of L3 lesion

COMPARISON:  Prior MRI liver done ___ and MRI L-spine done ___

PROCEDURE:  CT-guided L3 paravertebral body biopsy.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___, radiology trainee and Dr. ___,
___ radiologist. Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the
key components of the procedure and reviewed and agrees with the trainee's
findings.

TECHNIQUE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient.  After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a prone position on the CT scan table.  Limited
preprocedure CTscan of the intended biopsy area was performed.  Based on the
CT findings an appropriate position for the biopsy was chosen.  The site was
marked.

The site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine
were administered to the subcutaneous and deep tissues for local anesthetic
effect.  Under CT guidance, a 17 gauge coaxial needle was introduced into the
lesion.  An 18 gauge core biopsy device with a 22 mm throw was used to obtain
3 core biopsy specimens, which were sent for pathology.

The procedure was tolerated well and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

For a full description of diagnostic findings reference is made to report of
prior MRI liver done ___ and prior MRI L-spine done ___.

DOSE:   Total DLP (Body) = 530 mGy-cm.

SEDATION:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of 2
mg Versed and 75 mcg fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of 40
minutes during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.

FINDINGS:


1. 3 X 18 gauge biopsies performed of the L3 paravertebral body soft tissue.

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful CT-guided biopsy of the L3 paravertebral body soft
tissue.  Samples sent for pathology.
